newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-LOCKHART PINCH HOMER IN NINTH LIFTS BRAVES PAST EXPOS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-LOCKHART PINCH HOMER IN NINTH LIFTS BRAVES PAST EXPOS.

text.p: Keith Lockhart's two-run pinch homer with one out in the bottom of the ninth inning lifted the Atlanta Braves past the Montreal Expos 3-2 Wednesday for their sixth straight victory.

With Javy Lopez on second, Lockhart jumped on a 1-0 pitch from Ugueth Urbina (2-3) and drove it just inside the right-field foul pole for his first home run, ending the game. It was Urbina's second blown save in eight chances.

"Coming off the bench, you want to be aggressive, especially against a fastball pitcher," said Lockhart. "My job is to stay fit and loose. I really would've taken a base hit just to contribute to the team. It's nice to finally contribute to the team.
"I've never hit a home run to walk off the field like that, so I'll remember it."
The Expos lost for the first time in 22 games when leading entering the final inning.
Lockhart's homer made a winner of Greg Maddux (5-1), who threw a six-hitter for his second complete game of the season. He walked one and struck out six.
"You never know, there's always hope," said Maddux.
"I'm happy for Keith. I'm glad I got the win, don't get me wrong, but I'm happy for him."
Montreal lost for just the third time in its last 10 games.

Montreal scored two runs on a sacrifice fly in the seventh. Doug Strange flied out to Michael Tucker at the wall in right-centre field. Henry Rodriguez, who had singled, scored easily and rookie Vladimir Guerrero, who had doubled, never stopped and was able to slide home safely when Tony Graffanino's relay throw was to the right side of the plate.
It was the first time two runners scored on a sacrifice fly since April 5, 1996, when Brian Dorsett's fly ball scored Mark Grace and Sammy Sosa for the Cubs against the Dodgers.
In Houston, Luis Gonzalez's two-out single in the bottom of the 14th scored Jeff Bagwell with the winning run as the Astros beat the Cincinnati Reds 4-3.

Denis Menke, running the team in place of the suspended Ray Knight, had Bagwell intentionally walked for the third straight time. Bagwell stole second and scored when Gonzalez singled to left on a 3-2 pitch.
Scott Sullivan (0-1), Cincinnati's fifth pitcher, took the loss.
Tom Martin (2-1), celebrating his 27th birthday, earned the win with one inning of scoreless relief.

At Florida, Mark Clark allowed seven hits over eight innings and Edgardo Alfonzo and Bernard Gilkey hit solo homers to give the New York Mets a 2-1 victory over the Marlins, who had their eight-game winning streak snapped.

Clark (5-2) walked one and struck out five to run his scoreless streak to 16 innings. The right-hander retired 11 of the last 12 batters he faced before giving way to Greg McMichael, who allowed a run but notched his second save.
New York has won four of its last five games.
Al Leiter (3-3), making his first start since April 30, gave up a run and four hits over five innings.
In Chicago, Kevin Foster (5-3), Bob Patterson and Mel Rojas combined on a four-hitter and Sammy Sosa hit a two-run homer, his 10th, as the Cubs beat the Philadelphia Phillies 7-0.
The trio of Cubs pitchers allowed just five walks with six strikeouts as Chicago earned a two-game split. The Cubs finished their nine-game homestand at 6-3.

In San Francisco, Ellis Burks homered and drove in four runs and Kevin Ritz (4-4) pitched seven-plus innings for his first win in three weeks as the Colorado Rockies snapped a four-game skid with a 10-7 victory over the Giants.
Andres Galarraga added a two-run shot in the ninth for Colorado. He scored three times and surpassed Dave Concepcion as the all-time RBI leader (952) among Venezuelans.
Giants starter Kirk Rueter (2-1) took the loss.
In St Louis, Mark Johnson scored twice and doubled home the go-ahead run before being ejected as the Pittsburgh Pirates edged the Cardinals 3-2, snapping a four-game losing streak.

In the eighth, one batter after his game-winning RBI, Johnson rounded third too far and was caught in a rundown. He tried to score and lifted his elbow into catcher Mike Difelice as he was tagged out. A shoving match ensued and both dugouts emptied onto the field but order was quickly restored. Johnson and Difelice were ejected.
In San Diego, Quilvio Veras' groundout scored Chris Gomez with the winning run in the bottom of the 11th inning, lifting the San Diego Padres to a 5-4 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Trevor Hoffman (2-3) allowed one hit, walked one and struck three over two innings as the Padres secured their first three-game winning streak of the season and improved to 3-11 against opponents with winning records.
